title: A Physician's Case
author: a physician
pages: The carter was struck once, across the ribs, and walked home. No fever. He says he feels light, as if he had set something down.
Second day. He laughs in his sleep, quietly, and not like himself. His wife has moved to the other room.
I have no remedy in the books for this. The old women say gold, taken as leaf. I had him swallow a wedding ring's worth and he screamed that it burned.
Fourth day. He is heavy again and bad-tempered, and I have never been so glad of it.
